text: – That the Government continue to do what is necessary to facilitate access by operational police officers to the National database Person Profile system to enable checks to be conducted concerning a prisoner’s potential risk of self-harm. °    The Minimum Nationwide Person Profile (MNPP) system is still in the development stage across all police jurisdictions. Piloting in the SAPOL Records Response Unit is underway, with rollout expected in 2008. This system will provide officers with increased data rather than just the warnings that are presently available with Crimtrac. °    In February 2006 the Prisoner Screening Form (PD 331) was revised and, inter alia, provides a means to ensure the Police Information Management System (PI MS) and Crimtrac checks are undertaken as part of the prisoner charging process. General Orders also require the Crimtrac check is conducted through Records Response Unit when there is a belief that the prisoner has interstate antecedents. Albeit under trial at this stage, this gives officers access 24 hours a day to the 'fuller' MNPP data.

– That the holding cell facilities at the Elizabeth Cell Complex be upgraded to provide toilet and water facilities, together with more appropriate seating and emergency intercom devices. The facilities should incorporate a measure Annual Report of the State Coroner 2006-2007                                                          Page 25/38 of privacy which is consistent with the requirement to maintain adequate supervision. °    In August 2005, General Order - 'Prisoners', was revised to include strict directions with regard to the use of holding cells and holding areas. The amended General Order 'Prisoners' published directed that: •      Holding cells/holding areas are only to be used for the temporary confinement of a prisoner pending the prisoner being formally charged, where circumstances prevent the OIC from immediately undertaking the charging procedure, e.g. other prisoners in the process of being charged. •      A prisoner will not be placed in a holding cell/holding area at a police cell complex without the expressed permission of the OIC. – That on the assumption that the Government has no intention in the foreseeable future of providing funding for the upgrade of prison cells to comply with “safe cell” principles, the Minister for Correctional Services seek funding to convert a portion of the existing facilities in such a way as to provide safe and       humane   “special    needs”   units   in   each   custodial   institution   for   the accommodation of those prisoners requiring this type of management. °     The Department does not have designated 'special needs' units as recommended in the Coroner's report. Prisoners designated as 'at risk' and showing a potential to self harm may be placed either in Special Management Units or prison Infirmaries. These units provide a safe environment for prisoners, until such Annual Report of the State Coroner 2006-2007                                                            Page 30/38 time that they undergo any medical assessment and/or treatment, as may be required, prior to their return to the mainstream prison population. °    Following the deaths of Mr Turner and Mr Glennie, changes and improvements to the Department's self harm management system occurred to ensure that prisoners, who medical staff consider require daily assessment, could be easily identified and not overlooked. °    Specifically, the self harm notification forms have been replaced by an improved system that has addressed the issue of staff notification of high risk status. There is now a formal process in every institution to assess, monitor and implement management strategies for 'at risk' prisoners. Incumbent with this formal process is the ready exchange of information, both medical and custodial. – That all Correctional Service officers who have contact with prisoners in South Australian prisons and the Adelaide Remand Centre be provided with a Hoffman knife and have it in their possession ready for immediate use whenever they are working with prisoners. °    It is critical for the safety of all prisoners and staff that weapons be kept out of the hands of prisoners. Staff with potential weapons on their person, offer the ideal opportunity for prisoners to forcibly disarm them or steal their weapons and use them against other staff and prisoners. °    For that reason the Department, like many other correctional jurisdictions, does not allow weapons into a prison environment. °    If this policy was extended and knives were issued to all officers, as has been recommended by the Coroner, it would be very difficult to maintain the security of a prison.     Knives could be misplaced or stolen, and their presence in the hands of prisoners would present an even far greater safety risk to prisoners and staff. °    Given these circumstances, it is not the Department's intention to adopt the Coroner's recommendation in this instance. °    Notwithstanding, the Department recognises that there must be a balance between prisoner safety and security. The use of Hoffman knives in prison for use in cases of emergencies are therefore an exception to this policy.
